## Open

### T-085 — Drift still consumes the template-ref sequence, not the leg sequence

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · open_

Drift currently compares the ordered sequence of template refs of an execution (`FlowShapes` to
`flowVectorOf`). The sequence of legs is the more honest notion of "the flow's shape", because a
reword cannot disturb it, but switching the input changes R6c's observable behaviour and would leave
fault F3 ("hub rewords a message") with nothing to demonstrate, since a reword does not move the leg
sequence. The owner chose "compute both": the leg sequence and its vector are retained and exposed,
while drift keeps consuming the ref sequence. The open question is whether a leg-shape anomaly
should be added, and if it is, R6c's demonstration has to be re-founded.

### T-086 — Phases 2 to 4 of the semantic-log leg/diagram plan are still to do

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · open_

The plan of record is `/memories/session/plan.md` and the rulings are in
`.github/memory/decision.md`. Landed so far: `flow.leg` on the record model and rendered header;
`bindLeg`/`currentLeg`/`isLegId`; `src/propagation.ts` (`TRACE_HEADER`, `FLOW_HEADER`, `LEG_HEADER`,

Phase 2 is the mermaid diagram renderer, the three routes (`GET /flows`, `/flows/:kind/diagram`,

real-model test, and the inspector's `index`/`search` verbs over `vectors.jsonl`. Phase 4 is the R22
to R25 register rows with the R5/R9/R14 amendments, the three honesty checks with the fault-only
exemption list, and the docs: the flows page regenerated, the README event contract and routes, the
package `docs/`, and the both-ends instrumentation rule written down.

### T-087 — An unorderable leg pair is resolved by arrival order alone

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · open_

The ledger derives a leg's caller as the end whose record was emitted first, because a leg id names
a call site and encodes no endpoint (D8) and the caller's record precedes the call while the
callee's follows it. That works until the two records share a millisecond, which is ordinary on a
fast path: measured on the inter-scheme fixture, 7 of 14 legs tie. `LegEnd.tied` counts them, and
the pair is then resolved by arrival order alone, meaning by which service's sink flushed first. The
tie is reported rather than hidden, so no arrow is silently wrong, but a tie-broken arrow is still a
coin flip.

Three ways out, none free. (A) Accept it and let the diagram mark tied directions, which is what
ships now. (B) Make the pair sound by having the emitter carry a monotonic stamp it can compare
across two processes, which is an identity or wire change, and the clocks are still two clocks. (C)
Revisit D8 and let the id name its caller (`payer>hub/parties`), which needs one observation instead
of two and makes the tie disappear, at the cost of duplicating in the id what the call site already
says. Worth deciding before the diagram renderer is written, since (B) and (C) change what it draws.

### T-088 — The inspector's `index` and `search` verbs are missing

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · open_

This is the offline half of D22/D27. Semantic search is built and tested through `GET /search`
(templates plus retained records, with the real-model test proving a paraphrase finds the record it
means); what is missing is the `<dir>/vectors.jsonl` sidecar, its staleness rule and the "nothing
indexed" exit code. It is recorded in `core/semantic-log/docs/open-items.md` with the reasoning.

### T-089 — A legs-as-drift-shape anomaly has no founding case

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · open_

The per-execution call sequence is retained and published but is not a detector input: reworded
messages already fire drift (fault F3), so a second series would need its own founding case, a call
added, removed or reordered with the templates unchanged. It is recorded in
`core/semantic-log/docs/open-items.md`.
